title: Advanced Sterilization Products (ASP) STERRAD 100NX Sterilizer - Cycle Will Not Start, Aborts, or Fails During Conditioning
description: Troubleshoot cycle start, early abort, and conditioning failures caused by load, door, cassette, environmental, utility, or operating-state problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect Patient Care and Sterile Processing Workflow
steps.instructions: Do not rely on a sterilizer that cannot consistently start or complete a validated cycle. Quarantine any load from an incomplete or aborted cycle according to facility infection-prevention and sterile-processing procedures. Move required instruments to another verified sterilization pathway when available. Expected outcome: Patient-care continuity is maintained and no load from an incomplete cycle is released for clinical use. If an alternate validated sterilization process is available, continue troubleshooting the STERRAD 100NX out of clinical dependency.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Failure Point
steps.instructions: Review the operator report and determine whether the cycle: Will not begin after cycle selection Starts and immediately aborts Stops during conditioning Repeatedly returns to an earlier phase Produces a displayed message or alarm Fails only with certain loads or cycle selections Record the exact displayed message rather than interpreting or paraphrasing it. Expected outcome: The failure is narrowed to a repeatable stage or condition. If the problem was caused by an incorrect cycle selection or another clearly identified external operating condition and a subsequent test cycle completes normally, troubleshooting may stop after final verification.

steps.title: 3. Verify Power and Normal Startup
steps.instructions: Confirm the sterilizer is fully powered and has completed its normal startup sequence. Inspect the external power connection and verify there is no obvious loose plug, damaged cord, tripped local disconnect, or facility power disturbance. Do not repeatedly cycle power if the unit is freezing, restarting, producing unusual odor, overheating, or showing signs of electrical damage. Expected outcome: The system remains powered, stable, and ready for cycle selection without restarting or displaying a startup fault. If power is unstable, remove the unit from service until the electrical or equipment issue is corrected.

steps.title: 4. Check Door Closure and Chamber Obstructions
steps.instructions: Verify the door closes completely and no tray, packaging material, instrument, rack, or debris interferes with the seal or door mechanism. Inspect accessible door and chamber sealing surfaces for: Debris Packaging material Visible damage Moisture Distortion Objects preventing full closure Do not adjust or defeat the door interlock. Expected outcome: The door closes normally, the unit recognizes the closed condition, and the cycle can proceed. If correcting an external obstruction restores normal operation and a verification cycle completes successfully, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 5. Review Load Condition and Arrangement
steps.instructions: Verify the load is appropriate for the selected STERRAD process and is not obviously overloaded, densely packed, wet, or arranged in a way that could interfere with conditioning. Check that items were prepared and dried according to the applicable device and sterilization-processing instructions. Expected outcome: The chamber contains a dry, appropriately arranged load compatible with the selected cycle. If the failure occurs only with one improperly prepared load and a correctly prepared load completes normally, the problem is resolved.

steps.title: 6. Verify Hydrogen Peroxide Cassette Status
steps.instructions: Confirm that the cassette is properly installed and that the sterilizer recognizes it without repeated rejection or advance problems. Inspect accessible cassette areas for: Incorrect seating Packaging or debris interference Visible cassette damage Leakage Incorrect handling condition Do not bypass cassette recognition or manipulate internal delivery components. Expected outcome: The cassette is accepted and the sterilizer reports an available sterilant supply for the selected cycle. If cassette recognition remains abnormal, follow the dedicated cassette troubleshooting path or remove the unit from service as appropriate.

steps.title: 7. Check Chamber and Load for Moisture
steps.instructions: Conditioning may be interrupted when moisture is present. Inspect the chamber and load for visible water, condensation, damp packaging, wet lumens, or recently washed items that were not fully dried. Do not attempt to defeat moisture detection. Expected outcome: The chamber and load are visibly dry before a new cycle is attempted. If drying or removing the affected load allows the next cycle to complete normally, troubleshooting can stop after verifying repeatability.

steps.title: 8. Check Room and Installation Conditions
steps.instructions: Look for recent facility or environmental changes such as: HVAC interruption Excessive room heat High humidity Water intrusion near the sterilizer Construction activity Power disturbances Unit relocation Blocked external ventilation openings Maintain required clearances and do not obstruct cooling or ventilation paths. Expected outcome: No obvious environmental or installation condition is interfering with normal operation.

steps.title: 9. Perform a Controlled Verification Cycle
steps.instructions: After external causes are corrected, run an appropriate verification cycle following facility and manufacturer-approved procedures. Do not use patient-care instruments as the troubleshooting test load unless allowed by facility policy. Observe whether the unit passes conditioning and continues through the complete cycle without abnormal messages. Expected outcome: The sterilizer completes the verification cycle normally and produces an acceptable cycle record. If the cycle completes successfully and all required indicators and records are acceptable, troubleshooting can stop and the unit may proceed through normal return-to-service requirements.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Repeated Conditioning or Cycle Failures
steps.instructions: If the cycle still fails after power, door, load, cassette, moisture, and environment have been checked, stop repeated cycling. Repeated aborts may indicate a vacuum, sensing, sterilant-delivery, chamber, RF/plasma, software, or other service-level problem. Expected outcome: An unresolved sterilizer is removed from clinical use rather than repeatedly cycled without identifying the cause.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported that the STERRAD 100NX repeatedly aborted during the conditioning portion of the cycle.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found visible moisture on items in the load while the sterilizer itself powered, closed, and recognized the cassette normally.
CCR.Resolution: The wet load was removed, the chamber was confirmed dry, and a properly prepared verification load completed the full cycle successfully with an acceptable cycle record.

helpfulDetails: Whether the load was visibly dry
Recent facility power or HVAC event

title: Advanced Sterilization Products (ASP) STERRAD 100NX Sterilizer - Hydrogen Peroxide Cassette Not Recognized, Rejected, or Will Not Advance
description: Troubleshoot cassette recognition, rejection, seating, or advance problems caused by cassette condition, installation, obstruction, or sterilizer-side detection issues.

steps.title: 1. Protect Staff and Maintain Sterilization Availability
steps.instructions: Do not continue attempting to use a cassette that is damaged, leaking, or otherwise unsafe to handle. Follow facility procedures for hydrogen peroxide sterilant exposure and cassette handling. Move urgent instrument processing to another verified sterilization pathway when necessary. Expected outcome: Staff are protected from sterilant exposure and clinical processing can continue safely.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Cassette Complaint
steps.instructions: Determine whether the cassette: Is not detected Is immediately rejected Is accepted but will not advance Stops during use Produces a displayed message Works intermittently Fails only with one cassette Record the exact on-screen message. Expected outcome: The complaint is narrowed to recognition, acceptance, positioning, or movement.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Cassette Before Reinstallation
steps.instructions: Using appropriate handling precautions, visually inspect the cassette for: Physical damage Leakage Deformation Contamination Incorrect storage or handling condition Packaging material that should have been removed Any obvious reason it should not be used Do not use a visibly damaged or leaking cassette. Expected outcome: Only a cassette that appears suitable for use is installed. If the original cassette is clearly defective and another approved cassette is accepted normally, the issue is resolved after functional verification.

steps.title: 4. Verify Correct Cassette Installation
steps.instructions: Confirm the cassette is inserted in the correct orientation and fully seated according to the intended operator loading method. Do not force the cassette or manually manipulate internal advancement mechanisms. Expected outcome: The cassette seats normally without excessive resistance or misalignment. If reseating restores recognition and the system proceeds normally, continue to a complete cycle verification.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Accessible Cassette Area
steps.instructions: With the unit in a safe condition, inspect the accessible cassette loading area for: Debris Packaging fragments Foreign material Residue Visible mechanical obstruction Obvious physical damage Do not reach into inaccessible mechanisms or disassemble the cassette transport assembly. Expected outcome: The cassette path is externally clean and unobstructed. If removal of accessible debris restores normal cassette movement, verify operation before returning the unit to service.

steps.title: 6. Compare With a Known-Good Approved Cassette
steps.instructions: If permitted by facility procedures, test using another approved cassette that is known to be within acceptable use conditions. This comparison helps separate a cassette-specific problem from a sterilizer recognition or transport problem. Expected outcome: A known-good cassette is recognized and handled normally. If only one cassette fails, remove that cassette from use and manage it according to facility and manufacturer requirements.

steps.title: 7. Verify Door and System Readiness
steps.instructions: Confirm the sterilizer is otherwise in a normal ready state, the chamber door is properly closed when required, and there are no unrelated startup, door, or system faults preventing cassette processing. Expected outcome: No separate system condition is blocking cassette recognition or advancement.

steps.title: 8. Observe for Repeated Transport or Recognition Failure
steps.instructions: If multiple known-good cassettes are rejected, fail to advance, or are intermittently detected, stop repeated insertion attempts. Do not bypass sensors, manually advance the cassette, or access internal sterilant-delivery components. Expected outcome: A probable sterilizer-side problem is identified without creating additional risk or damage.

steps.title: 9. Perform Functional Verification After Correction
steps.instructions: If an external cause was corrected, run an appropriate verification cycle using approved procedures. Confirm the cassette remains recognized and advances as expected throughout the process. Expected outcome: The cassette is accepted and the sterilizer completes the verification cycle without cassette-related interruption. If successful, troubleshooting can stop after documenting the result.

steps.title: 10. Remove From Service for Persistent Cassette Handling Problems
steps.instructions: If multiple approved cassettes cannot be recognized or advanced, remove the sterilizer from service. Persistent failure may involve cassette detection, transport, sterilant delivery, control, or another internal service-level subsystem. Expected outcome: The sterilizer is prevented from entering clinical use with unreliable sterilant delivery.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported that the STERRAD 100NX rejected the installed hydrogen peroxide cassette and would not begin a cycle.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the cassette was not fully seated and no damage or obstruction was present in the accessible cassette area.
CCR.Resolution: The cassette was correctly reseated, recognized by the sterilizer, and a verification cycle completed successfully without cassette-related errors.

helpfulDetails: Whether cassette was detected or rejected

title: Advanced Sterilization Products (ASP) STERRAD 100NX Sterilizer - Vacuum Will Not Reach Target or Chamber Leak Suspected
description: Troubleshoot inadequate vacuum or suspected chamber leakage caused by door sealing, load condition, moisture, obstruction, installation, or service-level vacuum problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect Sterile Processing Workflow
steps.instructions: Do not release any load from a cycle that aborts because required processing conditions were not achieved. Move critical instrument processing to another validated sterilization pathway while the affected sterilizer is evaluated. Expected outcome: No incompletely processed load reaches patient care.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Vacuum-Related Symptom
steps.instructions: Determine whether the unit: Aborts during evacuation or conditioning Displays a vacuum- or pressure-related message Repeats evacuation attempts Behaves differently when empty versus loaded Makes unusual pumping sounds Shows evidence of a door or chamber sealing problem Record the exact message and cycle phase. Expected outcome: The complaint is confirmed as a repeatable evacuation or chamber-integrity problem.

steps.title: 3. Inspect Door Closure and Sealing Surfaces
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible door and chamber sealing surfaces for: Debris Packaging material Instrument contact Moisture Visible damage Distortion Contamination Confirm the door closes evenly without being forced. Do not alter the interlock or perform unauthorized seal adjustments. Expected outcome: The door closes completely and accessible sealing surfaces are clean and unobstructed. If correcting debris or an obstruction restores normal cycling, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 4. Check Chamber Loading
steps.instructions: Remove an obviously overloaded, poorly arranged, or oversized load and compare operation using an appropriate verification load. A load pressing against the door or interfering with normal chamber evacuation can mimic a sealing problem. Expected outcome: The load is appropriately positioned and does not interfere with the chamber or door. If the problem disappears with proper loading and a full verification cycle completes, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 5. Inspect for Moisture
steps.instructions: Check the chamber, trays, packaging, and instruments for visible moisture or condensation. Moisture can interfere with the conditioning and evacuation process and may produce symptoms that appear similar to a vacuum problem. Expected outcome: The chamber and test load are visibly dry.

steps.title: 6. Check External Ventilation and Environment
steps.instructions: Verify the sterilizer has not recently been moved and that required external clearances and ventilation openings are not blocked. Review whether there was a recent facility power, HVAC, construction, or environmental event associated with the onset of the problem. Expected outcome: No obvious installation or environmental factor is contributing to abnormal operation.

steps.title: 7. Compare Empty or Approved Test Operation
steps.instructions: When permitted by manufacturer and facility procedures, perform an approved verification cycle or diagnostic functional check that helps distinguish load-related behavior from a sterilizer-side evacuation problem. Do not access internal vacuum components. Expected outcome: The sterilizer achieves normal cycle progression under approved test conditions. If the unit functions normally under the verification condition and the original load problem is corrected, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 8. Listen and Inspect for Obvious External Signs
steps.instructions: During an approved test cycle, observe for: Unusual vacuum pump sound Repeated evacuation attempts Air movement around the door New vibration Unusual odor Visible door movement Fluid leakage Do not continue operating if there is evidence of overheating, electrical damage, chemical leakage, or other unsafe behavior. Expected outcome: No abnormal external sign indicates a significant mechanical or safety problem.

steps.title: 9. Stop Repeated Cycling if Vacuum Cannot Be Achieved
steps.instructions: If multiple appropriately prepared verification attempts fail after the door, chamber, load, and moisture checks, stop cycling the sterilizer. Repeated operation will not correct a persistent leak or vacuum-system problem. Expected outcome: An unresolved sterilizer is removed from use before additional failed loads occur.

steps.title: 10. Escalate for Service-Level Evaluation
steps.instructions: A persistent vacuum problem may involve chamber sealing, vacuum generation, valves, pressure measurement, tubing, control, or another internal subsystem. These are service-level conditions requiring approved procedures and test equipment. Expected outcome: The problem is escalated without unauthorized internal repair.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported that the STERRAD 100NX repeatedly aborted during evacuation and appeared unable to establish adequate chamber vacuum.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found packaging material trapped on the accessible door sealing surface and interfering with complete closure.
CCR.Resolution: The obstruction was removed, the sealing area was inspected and cleaned, and an approved verification cycle completed normally without further vacuum-related failure.

title: Advanced Sterilization Products (ASP) STERRAD 100NX Sterilizer - Moisture Detection Prevents Cycle Completion
description: Troubleshoot moisture-related cycle interruption caused by wet instruments, damp packaging, condensation, chamber moisture, or persistent sensing and vacuum problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Load and Maintain Processing Continuity
steps.instructions: Do not release instruments from a moisture-interrupted or otherwise incomplete cycle. Move urgent loads to another approved sterilization pathway if available. Expected outcome: Patient-use instruments remain limited to loads that have completed a validated process.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Moisture-Related Condition
steps.instructions: Review the exact displayed message and determine when the cycle stops. Ask whether the problem: Occurs with every load Occurs only with certain instrument sets Began after washing or rapid turnaround Occurs after a particular tray or lumen device is loaded Persists with an otherwise dry verification load Expected outcome: The moisture event is correlated with either the load or the sterilizer.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Load for Visible Moisture
steps.instructions: Examine instruments, trays, packaging, lumens, hinges, cavities, and other areas where water can remain trapped. Do not assume the load is dry simply because exterior surfaces appear dry. Expected outcome: All items intended for processing are visibly dry and were prepared using the applicable instructions. If wet items are found, remove and dry them appropriately before retesting.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Chamber and Accessories
steps.instructions: Check accessible chamber surfaces, trays, and racks for: Condensation Water droplets Damp surfaces Residual cleaning fluid Wet accessories Recent spill or cleaning activity Expected outcome: The chamber and loading accessories are dry before the next cycle.

steps.title: 5. Check Load Density and Arrangement
steps.instructions: Verify that the load is not packed so densely that moisture remains trapped or normal chamber conditioning is impaired. Check that instruments and packaging are positioned according to applicable processing requirements. Expected outcome: The load is appropriately arranged and permits normal processing.

steps.title: 6. Identify Load-Specific Patterns
steps.instructions: If the problem is intermittent, compare: One instrument set versus another One tray versus another Lumen versus non-lumen items Recently washed versus fully dried items Avoid repeated full loads until the pattern is understood. Expected outcome: A specific load, tray, or preparation condition is either identified or ruled out. If one load consistently causes the problem while approved dry verification loads do not, troubleshooting can stop after the load-processing cause is corrected and verified.

steps.title: 7. Check Room Conditions
steps.instructions: Review whether unusually high room humidity, temperature changes, HVAC interruptions, or cold instruments entering a warmer environment could be contributing to condensation. Do not alter sterilizer configuration to compensate for an uncontrolled room condition. Expected outcome: The sterilizer is operating in a stable environment without obvious condensation-producing conditions.

steps.title: 8. Run an Appropriate Dry Verification Load
steps.instructions: Once visible moisture and load preparation issues are corrected, run an approved verification cycle with a properly prepared dry load. Expected outcome: The unit completes the full cycle without a moisture-related interruption. If successful and the problem does not recur, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 9. Compare Persistent Moisture Events With Other Symptoms
steps.instructions: If dry verification loads still fail, determine whether there are also: Vacuum failures Repeated conditioning attempts Door sealing concerns Unusual chamber behavior Other system messages This can indicate that the apparent moisture problem is related to a broader vacuum, sensing, or system condition. Expected outcome: A persistent sterilizer-side problem is identified for escalation rather than repeated load adjustments.

steps.title: 10. Remove From Service if Dry Loads Continue to Fail
steps.instructions: If the moisture condition occurs with verified dry loads after external causes are ruled out, remove the sterilizer from service. Do not bypass moisture detection or attempt unauthorized sensor adjustment. Expected outcome: An unreliable sterilization process is prevented from returning to patient-use workflow.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported repeated moisture-related cycle interruptions on the STERRAD 100NX.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found residual water in a recently washed instrument tray while the sterilizer chamber was dry and otherwise operated normally.
CCR.Resolution: The wet tray was removed and fully dried, and a properly prepared verification load completed the full sterilization cycle successfully.

title: Advanced Sterilization Products (ASP) STERRAD 100NX Sterilizer - Door Will Not Open, Close, Lock, or Seal
description: Troubleshoot door movement, closure, locking, and sealing problems caused by obstruction, load interference, contamination, alignment, or service-level interlock issues.

steps.title: 1. Protect Staff and the Processed Load
steps.instructions: Do not force the door open or closed. If a cycle was interrupted, treat the load as unprocessed until it has completed an approved sterilization cycle. If the chamber may contain residual sterilant from an abnormal cycle, follow facility safety procedures before handling the load. Expected outcome: Staff and instruments remain protected while the door problem is evaluated.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Door Symptom
steps.instructions: Determine whether the door: Will not open Will not close Closes but is not recognized Will not lock Will not unlock Appears to leak Stops partway through movement Fails only after a cycle Record any displayed message. Expected outcome: The complaint is narrowed to movement, recognition, locking, unlocking, or sealing.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Unit Is in a Safe Operating State
steps.instructions: Confirm the sterilizer has completed or safely terminated its current process and is not still actively controlling the chamber. Do not defeat an interlock to access the chamber. Expected outcome: The door is being evaluated only when the sterilizer is in a state where door operation should normally be permitted.

steps.title: 4. Inspect for Load or Packaging Obstruction
steps.instructions: Look around the accessible door opening for: Trays extending too far Instruments contacting the door Packaging caught between surfaces Loose wraps Labels or debris Foreign material Expected outcome: Nothing physically interferes with door travel or closure. If the obstruction is removed and normal door operation returns, continue to cycle verification.

steps.title: 5. Inspect Accessible Door and Sealing Surfaces
steps.instructions: Inspect for: Debris Residue Moisture Visible gasket or sealing-surface damage Distortion Cracking Contamination Clean only according to approved procedures. Expected outcome: Accessible sealing surfaces are clean, intact, and unobstructed.

steps.title: 6. Check for Uneven or Forced Movement
steps.instructions: Operate the door only through its normal intended controls or manual interaction. Do not pry, strike, or force it. Observe whether movement is smooth and whether one side appears to bind. Expected outcome: The door moves normally without abnormal resistance, binding, or misalignment. If significant binding or mechanical misalignment is evident, remove the unit from service.

steps.title: 7. Verify Door Recognition
steps.instructions: After proper closure, confirm the sterilizer recognizes the required door state. If the door is physically closed but the system does not recognize it, do not defeat or adjust sensors without authorized service procedures. Expected outcome: Physical door position and displayed/system door status agree.

steps.title: 8. Check Whether the Problem Is Cycle-Dependent
steps.instructions: Determine whether the door works normally when idle but fails to unlock after a cycle or whether it fails at all times. A post-cycle-only problem may indicate a chamber, control, vacuum, or interlock condition rather than a simple mechanical obstruction. Expected outcome: The failure pattern is clearly documented for further diagnosis or escalation.

steps.title: 9. Perform Functional Verification After Correction
steps.instructions: If an external obstruction or contamination was corrected, verify normal opening, closing, locking, and cycle operation using approved procedures. Expected outcome: The door operates correctly through the full cycle sequence without abnormal messages or leakage. If verified, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Remove From Service for Persistent Door or Interlock Failure
steps.instructions: Remove the unit from service if the door: Cannot be reliably secured Cannot be released normally Binds or appears damaged Is not correctly recognized Appears unable to seal Requires force to operate Expected outcome: A sterilizer with unreliable chamber containment or interlock protection is not used clinically.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported that the STERRAD 100NX door would not close completely and the cycle could not be started.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found a portion of load packaging extending into the door sealing area and preventing full closure.
CCR.Resolution: The packaging obstruction was removed, the door and sealing surfaces were inspected, and the sterilizer completed a verification cycle with normal locking and unlocking.

helpfulDetails: Whether problem occurs only after cycles

title: Advanced Sterilization Products (ASP) STERRAD 100NX Sterilizer - Plasma Generation or RF System Failure
description: Troubleshoot plasma or RF-related cycle failures by ruling out power, load, moisture, chamber, door, and repeatable external conditions before service escalation.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Load and Remove Clinical Dependency
steps.instructions: A cycle that does not complete its required sterilization phases must not be considered successful. Quarantine the affected load and move urgent processing to another validated method. Expected outcome: No incompletely processed instruments are released for patient use.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Failure
steps.instructions: Determine: Exact displayed message Phase where the failure occurs Whether the cycle always reaches the same point Whether all cycle types are affected Whether the failure began after power interruption, maintenance, relocation, or an unusual load Do not assume an RF failure based only on an interrupted cycle unless the unit specifically indicates that system. Expected outcome: The failure is accurately characterized before internal failure is suspected.

steps.title: 3. Verify Stable AC Power and Normal Startup
steps.instructions: Check that the unit powers normally, completes startup, and remains stable. Inspect the external power connection for obvious damage or looseness and determine whether recent facility power disturbances occurred. Expected outcome: The sterilizer has stable power and no unrelated startup abnormality. If power is unstable, correct the facility or external power condition before further testing.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Load for Moisture and Improper Preparation
steps.instructions: A wet or unsuitable load may interrupt processing before or during phases associated with plasma generation. Verify items are dry, compatible, and prepared appropriately. Expected outcome: The verification load is dry and properly prepared.

steps.title: 5. Verify Chamber Loading and Clearance
steps.instructions: Check that the chamber is not overloaded and that trays, instruments, or packaging are not contacting areas they should not contact or obstructing normal chamber conditions. Expected outcome: Load placement is appropriate and does not create an obvious external reason for cycle interruption.

steps.title: 6. Verify Door Closure and Chamber Condition
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible door sealing surfaces and the chamber for debris, moisture, damage, or obstruction. A vacuum or chamber-integrity problem can prevent the sterilizer from reaching later cycle phases. Expected outcome: The chamber and door appear normal externally and the unit can proceed through earlier cycle phases.

steps.title: 7. Verify Cassette Acceptance
steps.instructions: Confirm the hydrogen peroxide cassette is recognized and the sterilizer does not have a separate cassette or sterilant-delivery problem. Expected outcome: The cassette is accepted and no independent cassette fault explains the interrupted cycle.

steps.title: 8. Repeat Only With an Approved Verification Condition
steps.instructions: After correcting any external issues, perform an approved verification cycle. Do not repeatedly expose full clinical loads to failed cycles while attempting to determine whether the RF/plasma system will recover. Expected outcome: The verification cycle progresses through all required phases and completes successfully. If the cycle completes normally and the corrected external cause does not recur, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 9. Stop if the RF/Plasma Failure Repeats
steps.instructions: If the same RF/plasma-related failure returns with a correctly prepared verification load and external causes are ruled out, stop further cycling. Do not open RF assemblies, adjust internal generators, access high-voltage components, or perform board-level troubleshooting. Expected outcome: A likely service-level failure is identified without unsafe internal access.

steps.title: 10. Escalate to Qualified Service
steps.instructions: Persistent plasma or RF faults may involve RF generation, matching, sensing, electrical control, chamber conditions, vacuum performance, or related internal circuitry. Expected outcome: The device is removed from use and transferred for qualified evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported repeated STERRAD 100NX cycle failures when the unit reached the plasma portion of processing.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering verified stable power, a dry approved test load, proper door closure, and normal cassette recognition, but the plasma-related failure repeated.
CCR.Resolution: The sterilizer was removed from service, labeled Out of Service, and referred for ASP-qualified service evaluation before any return to clinical use.

title: Advanced Sterilization Products (ASP) STERRAD 100NX Sterilizer - Cycle Takes Longer Than Expected or Repeats a Phase
description: Troubleshoot unexpectedly long cycles or repeated phases caused by load preparation, moisture, chamber conditions, vacuum performance, or developing system problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect Sterile Processing Workflow
steps.instructions: If the cycle eventually completes normally and all required indicators are acceptable, do not assume a sterilization failure solely because staff perceived it as slow. However, if the unit repeatedly stalls, aborts, or behaves unpredictably, move urgent processing to another verified sterilizer. Expected outcome: Patient-care workflow continues without relying on an unreliable sterilization process.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Actual Cycle Behavior
steps.instructions: Determine: Cycle selected Expected versus observed workflow Which phase appears prolonged Whether a phase truly repeats Whether the cycle completes successfully Whether the condition affects all loads Exact messages shown during the delay Use available cycle records when appropriate rather than relying only on recollection. Expected outcome: The complaint is confirmed as an actual process change rather than normal variation or an incorrect cycle selection.

steps.title: 3. Verify Correct Cycle Selection
steps.instructions: Confirm the selected cycle is appropriate for the load and that staff are comparing it with the same cycle type previously used. Do not alter protected configuration values simply to shorten a cycle. Expected outcome: The correct process was selected and the time comparison is valid.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Load Size and Arrangement
steps.instructions: Review whether the load is larger, denser, more complex, or differently arranged than typical loads. Check for: Excessive load density Closely packed trays Unusual instrument combinations Packaging that restricts normal conditioning Chamber contact Expected outcome: The load is appropriate for the selected cycle and arranged correctly.

steps.title: 5. Check for Moisture
steps.instructions: Inspect instruments, trays, packaging, and chamber surfaces for residual moisture. A system may spend additional time attempting to establish acceptable process conditions when a load is not fully dry. Expected outcome: The chamber and load are visibly dry. If correcting load moisture restores normal cycle behavior, troubleshooting can stop after successful verification.

steps.title: 6. Verify Door Closure and Chamber Sealing Surfaces
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible door sealing surfaces for debris, packaging, residue, or visible damage. Minor sealing interference may cause repeated evacuation or conditioning attempts. Expected outcome: The door closes normally and sealing surfaces are unobstructed.

steps.title: 7. Review Vacuum-Related Behavior
steps.instructions: Observe whether the longer cycle appears associated with: Repeated evacuation Extended conditioning Vacuum-related messages Unusual pumping sounds Do not access internal vacuum components during external troubleshooting. Expected outcome: Either normal evacuation behavior is confirmed or a probable vacuum/chamber issue is identified for escalation.

steps.title: 8. Check Environmental and Facility Changes
steps.instructions: Determine whether the issue began after: HVAC interruption High room humidity Power disturbance Sterilizer relocation Construction Service work Changes in load-processing workflow Expected outcome: No obvious environmental or workflow change explains the longer cycles.

steps.title: 9. Run a Controlled Verification Cycle
steps.instructions: Use an appropriate approved test or verification load after correcting external causes. Compare its operation with the reported condition. Expected outcome: The sterilizer progresses normally through the selected cycle without repeated phases or abnormal delay. If normal operation returns, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Process Delays
steps.instructions: If the sterilizer repeatedly extends or repeats phases with proper loads and no obvious external cause, remove it from service for evaluation. Possible categories include vacuum, sensing, chamber conditions, sterilant delivery, control software, or another service-level subsystem. Expected outcome: An increasingly unreliable sterilizer is serviced before it begins aborting loads or producing uncertain process performance.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported that STERRAD 100NX cycles were taking longer than usual and appeared to repeat conditioning.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found several instruments in the reported load were still visibly damp after cleaning and drying.
CCR.Resolution: The load was removed and fully dried, and a properly prepared verification load completed normally without repeated conditioning.

title: Advanced Sterilization Products (ASP) STERRAD 100NX Sterilizer - Printer, Barcode Scanner, USB, or Cycle Record Failure
description: Troubleshoot cycle-documentation and peripheral failures involving printing, barcode scanning, USB transfer, or missing records before assuming internal control failure.

steps.title: 1. Protect Traceability and Sterile Processing Records
steps.instructions: Do not ignore missing cycle documentation when the facility depends on it for sterilization traceability or load release. Follow facility procedures for manual documentation or alternate record capture while troubleshooting. Expected outcome: Instrument processing remains traceable even while a peripheral or documentation function is unavailable.

steps.title: 2. Identify the Exact Function That Failed
steps.instructions: Determine whether the problem involves: Printer output Paper feeding Barcode scanner input USB recognition USB export Missing stored cycle record Incomplete record Multiple functions simultaneously Expected outcome: The failure is narrowed to one peripheral, storage/export function, or a broader system issue.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Sterilization Cycle Itself Completed Normally
steps.instructions: Confirm whether the cycle successfully completed and whether only the documentation function failed. Do not confuse a peripheral failure with a failed sterilization process. Expected outcome: The clinical significance of the problem is understood: process failure versus documentation failure.

steps.title: 4. Check External Peripheral Connections
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible external cables and connectors for: Loose connections Bent or damaged plugs Pinched cables Contamination Strain Unapproved adapters Reseat user-accessible connectors only when safe and intended for normal external connection. Expected outcome: All peripheral connections are secure and undamaged.

steps.title: 5. Check Printer Consumables and Basic Condition
steps.instructions: For printer complaints, verify accessible consumables and normal paper loading. Inspect for obvious jams, damaged paper, or a cover that is not fully closed. Do not disassemble the printer mechanism beyond normal accessible areas. Expected outcome: The printer has usable media and no obvious external jam or loading problem.

steps.title: 6. Check Barcode Scanner Condition
steps.instructions: Inspect the scanner window and cable for contamination or damage. Test an approved, clearly printed barcode that is known to scan elsewhere if available. Expected outcome: A known-good barcode is read reliably. If cleaning an accessible scanner window or reseating the connection restores scanning, verify the function and troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 7. Check USB Device and Port Externally
steps.instructions: For USB problems, verify the approved device is correctly inserted and not physically damaged. If facility policy allows, compare with another known-good approved USB device. Do not use unknown personal storage media on clinical equipment. Expected outcome: The sterilizer detects the approved USB device and can complete the intended export function.

steps.title: 8. Verify Record Availability on the Sterilizer
steps.instructions: Determine whether the cycle record is visible or stored locally even though it cannot print or export. This helps separate record-generation problems from printer or USB problems. Expected outcome: The record either exists locally, indicating a peripheral/export issue, or is also missing, indicating a broader documentation problem.

steps.title: 9. Restart Only When Operationally Appropriate
steps.instructions: If the device is idle and facility procedures allow, perform a normal controlled restart to clear a transient peripheral interface problem. Do not power-cycle during an active cycle or while record-writing activity is underway. Expected outcome: The sterilizer returns to normal operation and the affected peripheral function is restored. If the failure clears and a new verification record prints, scans, or exports normally, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Documentation or Peripheral Failure
steps.instructions: If known-good external devices and connections do not resolve the issue, remove the affected peripheral function from use and determine whether the sterilizer itself must be removed from service based on facility traceability requirements. Possible service-level categories include interface electronics, internal printer hardware, storage, operating software, or control-system communication. Expected outcome: Required sterilization documentation is not compromised by continuing to operate an inadequately documented system.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported that the STERRAD 100NX completed cycles normally but would not print the cycle record.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the printer paper was incorrectly loaded while the stored cycle record remained available on the sterilizer.
CCR.Resolution: The printer media was reloaded correctly and a subsequent verification cycle produced a complete printed record.

title: Advanced Sterilization Products (ASP) STERRAD 100NX Sterilizer - Network Connection or Instrument Tracking Integration Failure
description: Troubleshoot network or tracking integration loss caused by cabling, switch connectivity, configuration, infrastructure, or interface-system problems without altering protected settings.

steps.title: 1. Protect Sterile Processing Traceability
steps.instructions: Determine whether loss of network or tracking integration affects load release, documentation, or instrument traceability. Use the facility-approved manual or alternate workflow when necessary. Expected outcome: Sterilization records and instrument traceability are maintained despite the connectivity outage.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Scope of the Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether: Only one STERRAD 100NX is affected Multiple sterile-processing devices are affected The sterilizer shows offline status The instrument tracking system is unavailable globally Cycle data is generated locally but not transmitted Connectivity is intermittent Expected outcome: The issue is narrowed to the sterilizer, local network path, or enterprise application.

steps.title: 3. Verify Local Sterilizer Operation
steps.instructions: Confirm the sterilizer itself powers normally, completes cycles, and creates local cycle records. A network problem should not be assumed to be a sterilizer process failure. Expected outcome: The sterilization process and local record generation are either confirmed normal or identified as a separate issue.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Network Cable and Port
steps.instructions: Inspect the external Ethernet cable for damage, loose seating, broken latch tabs, sharp bends, or strain. Verify both ends are connected to the intended ports. Expected outcome: The physical network connection is secure and undamaged. If reseating a loose cable restores connectivity and data flow, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 5. Check Link Indicators When Available
steps.instructions: Observe normal external network link/activity indications on the device or network connection if visible. Compare with a known-working nearby device when useful. Expected outcome: A physical Ethernet link is present. No link with a known-good cable suggests a port, jack, switch, or device-interface problem requiring further isolation.

steps.title: 6. Test With a Known-Good Network Path When Authorized
steps.instructions: If local IT/Clinical Engineering procedures allow, compare the cable, wall jack, or switch path with a known-working connection without changing protected network configuration. Avoid moving the sterilizer onto an arbitrary network or VLAN. Expected outcome: The problem is isolated to the device-side connection or facility network infrastructure.

steps.title: 7. Verify Observed Network Configuration
steps.instructions: Review, but do not arbitrarily change, approved network settings such as device address information or server destination values if these are accessible within authorized technical scope. Compare them with documented approved values. Expected outcome: The observed configuration matches the known approved configuration. If it does not, escalate before making changes unless Clinical Engineering is specifically authorized to restore the documented configuration.

steps.title: 8. Check the Instrument Tracking System
steps.instructions: Determine whether the receiving tracking application, server, interface engine, or related hospital system is operational. Ask IT or the application owner whether there is an active outage or maintenance event. Expected outcome: The upstream receiving system is confirmed available or an infrastructure outage is identified.

steps.title: 9. Verify End-to-End Data Flow
steps.instructions: After correcting an external network issue, verify that a new test or approved cycle record reaches the intended destination and is associated correctly. Do not consider link restoration alone sufficient if the clinical requirement is actual data transfer. Expected outcome: New cycle data successfully traverses the complete path from sterilizer to the intended tracking system. If verified, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Connectivity Failure
steps.instructions: If cabling, local link, approved configuration, and receiving-system availability have been checked, escalate to the appropriate ASP, Clinical Engineering, IT networking, cybersecurity, or integration support team. Expected outcome: The unresolved issue is routed to the team responsible for the failing layer rather than addressed through unauthorized configuration changes.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported that completed STERRAD 100NX cycle records were no longer appearing in the instrument tracking system.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the sterilizer was functioning normally but the external Ethernet cable was loose and the network link was down.
CCR.Resolution: The network cable was reseated, link was restored, and a new verification record successfully transferred to the instrument tracking system.

helpfulDetails: Wall jack or switch port tested

title: Advanced Sterilization Products (ASP) STERRAD 100NX Sterilizer - Display, Touchscreen, Foot Pedal, or Startup Failure
description: Troubleshoot startup and user-interface failures involving the display, touchscreen, foot pedal, external power, connections, or system control before service escalation.

steps.title: 1. Protect Clinical Workflow and Do Not Use an Unreliable Control Interface
steps.instructions: Do not operate the sterilizer if staff cannot reliably view status, select required functions, or control the unit. Move instrument processing to another verified sterilizer if necessary. Expected outcome: The sterilization process does not depend on a partially functional control interface.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Symptom
steps.instructions: Determine whether the issue is: No power Blank display Frozen startup screen Repeated restart Touchscreen not responding Only part of the touchscreen responding Foot pedal not responding Display visible but controls unavailable Failure only after startup Expected outcome: The issue is separated into power, display, touch input, accessory input, or software/startup behavior.

steps.title: 3. Verify External Power
steps.instructions: Inspect the power cord, plug, and connection for obvious damage or looseness. Confirm the facility outlet or supply is available using approved methods and determine whether a breaker, disconnect, or facility outage is involved. Do not repeatedly reset a breaker that continues to trip. Expected outcome: Stable external power is available to the sterilizer. If restoring a facility power connection resolves the issue and startup completes normally, continue to final functional verification.

steps.title: 4. Observe the Startup Sequence
steps.instructions: Power the sterilizer normally and observe: Whether indicators activate Whether the display illuminates Whether startup progresses Whether the unit freezes at a consistent point Whether it restarts unexpectedly Whether an exact message appears Do not access service menus or interrupt software initialization unnecessarily. Expected outcome: Startup either completes normally or a repeatable failure point is identified.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Display and Touchscreen Externally
steps.instructions: Check for: Cracks Liquid intrusion Contamination Protective material interfering with touch Impact damage Delamination Unresponsive areas Clean only using approved methods. Expected outcome: The user interface is physically intact and free of external contamination that could interfere with operation.

steps.title: 6. Check the Foot Pedal and External Connection
steps.instructions: If the complaint involves the foot pedal, inspect the pedal and accessible cable/connector for: Damage Loose connection Pinching Fluid contamination Strain Bent or damaged connector features Reseat the connector if it is intended to be externally removable. Expected outcome: The foot pedal is securely connected and free of obvious damage. If reseating or replacing a damaged external accessory with an approved known-good unit restores function, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 7. Compare With a Known-Good Accessory When Available
steps.instructions: For a removable foot pedal or other approved external control accessory, compare with a known-good compatible unit if available. Do not substitute unapproved accessories. Expected outcome: The fault is isolated to the accessory or the sterilizer interface.

steps.title: 8. Perform a Controlled Restart if Appropriate
steps.instructions: If the unit is idle and no cycle is active, perform a normal shutdown and restart using approved procedures. Do not repeatedly power-cycle a unit that is continuously restarting, overheating, or showing electrical abnormality. Expected outcome: A transient interface or startup condition clears and the system starts normally. If normal operation returns, continue with a full functional check before release.

steps.title: 9. Verify Complete User Interface Function
steps.instructions: After any correction, confirm: Startup completes Display remains stable Required touch controls respond Foot pedal operates if applicable Cycle selection can be performed normally No repeated restart occurs Run an approved verification cycle when required. Expected outcome: The user interface remains reliable through normal operation and the verification cycle completes successfully. If all functions pass, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Remove From Service for Persistent Startup or Control Failure
steps.instructions: Remove the sterilizer from service if it: Will not complete startup Repeatedly restarts Has an unreliable touchscreen Has a blank or unreadable display Cannot reliably accept operator input Shows evidence of fluid intrusion, overheating, electrical damage, or internal failure Expected outcome: An unreliable control system is prevented from affecting sterilization operation or load processing.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported that the STERRAD 100NX display powered on but the foot pedal did not respond during normal operation.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the external foot-pedal connector was partially disengaged and the cable showed no physical damage.
CCR.Resolution: The connector was fully reseated, foot-pedal operation was verified, and the sterilizer completed an approved functional verification cycle normally.
